Subject: Request: Private colo peering & transit SLA

Sofia —

Thanks for taking this. We're currently standing up private colo peering with Redwood in our New York and SJC facilities. Our ops team has identified a few cases where on-prem transit (customer-managed cross-connects and our colo transit provider) will be the root cause for latency spikes or intermittent packet loss. Given that those pieces are under PrismEdge control, we need an explicit carveout in the SLA for availability/latency attribution and a short list of evidence items Redwood will accept to close incidents.

High-level asks from our side:
- A clear clause stating network/transit under customer control is excluded from Redwood uptime calculations (or a defined attribution procedure).
- A list of technical evidence Redwood will accept to attribute incidents: traceroutes/MTRs, BGP session logs, colo port status, timestamps from our NMS.
- A defined expected turnaround for Redwood to review submitted evidence (we'd like 48h initial triage).

We can share network diagrams and sample MTRs — attaching a simplified topology and an example MTR output.

Would appreciate your confirmation on what Redwood needs to accept the carveout and whether legal needs a proposed redline.

Thanks,
Liam O'Neill
NetOps Lead, PrismEdge Inc
(liam.oneill@prismedge.com)

Attachments: network-diagram-v1.pdf, prismedge-mtr-sample.txt

Sofia / team —

Thanks — below is a proposed approach that balances operational clarity with our risk posture. High level: Redwood will accept a bounded set of artifacts for attribution and will perform an initial triage within 48 hours of receipt. The deeper forensic work (if required) will be scoped and may take longer.

Proposed evidence Redwood will accept (minimum):
- MTR/traceroute outputs from both sides showing path and latency distribution (plain text).
- BGP session logs or BGP4 show outputs showing session up/down timestamps.
- Colo cross-connect port status (carrier/colo ticket ID + port up/down events).
- If available, sample tcpdump/pcap excerpt (first-party redacted) for packet-loss verification — accept only if transmitted securely.

Proposed SLA language snippet for redline (draft):
"Private transit and network components that are provisioned, operated, or controlled by the Customer (including but not limited to cross-connects, transit VLANs, third-party colo transit, and Customer-managed routers) shall be out of scope for Redwood's Service Availability calculations, subject to the Customer providing the attestation artifacts listed in Appendix X. Upon receipt of such artifacts, Redwood will complete an initial evidence triage within 48 hours to determine attribution. If further forensic analysis is required, Redwood will notify the Customer and provide an estimated timeline for completion."

Operational notes:
- Require NTP-aligned timestamps (within 5s) on logs MTR outputs to avoid clock drift disputes.
- Accept gzip/plain text for larger captures; prefer sha256 digests for any uploaded pcap excerpts.
- For production incidents where PrismEdge asks for SLA credit, require both MTR evidence and either BGP or colo ticket evidence (two corroborating sources).

I'll attach a redline doc with this snippet plus a short Appendix X checklist for Legal to review. Naomi — any security/PII concerns with accepting pcaps?

Karthik
Engineering Lead, Infra Ops
